question: Which promised son am I?
reference: Genesis 21-27 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Isaac')

clues: I was born when my father was 100 and my mother about 90.
As a boy I carried the wood up a mountain where I was nearly offered as a sacrifice.
My father's servant chose a wife for me, Rebekah, and met her at a well.
In my old age I was tricked into blessing my younger son instead of the elder.

question: Which first high priest am I?
reference: Exodus 4-7; 32; Numbers 17; 20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Aaron')

clues: I was my brother's spokesman before Pharaoh.
My staff became a serpent, and later it alone budded and produced almonds.
While my brother was on the mountain, I made a golden calf for the people.
I was not allowed into the Promised Land, and I died on Mount Hor.

question: Which sister of a leader am I?
reference: Exodus 2; 15; Numbers 12; 20 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Miriam No. 1')

clues: I watched my baby brother float among the reeds and arranged for our own mother to nurse him.
After the crossing of the sea, I led the women with tambourines and dancing.
I spoke against my brother's wife and was struck with leprosy for seven days.
I died at Kadesh, and there was no water for the people there.

question: Which vow-making judge am I?
reference: Judges 11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jephthah')

clues: As the son of a prostitute, I was driven out by my half-brothers.
When the Ammonites threatened war, the elders begged me to come back and lead.
I vowed to offer up whatever came out of my house to meet me if I returned in victory.
My only child, a daughter, came out to greet me with tambourines.

question: Which kinsman-redeemer am I?
reference: Ruth 2-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Boaz')

clues: I was a well-to-do landowner in Bethlehem during the days of the judges.
I told my harvesters to leave extra grain for a young widow gleaning in my field.
I settled the question of redemption at the city gate, sealed by the handing over of a sandal.
I married Ruth, and we became the great-grandparents of King David.

question: Which high priest of Shiloh am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 1-4 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Eli')

clues: I mistook a silently praying woman at the sanctuary for a drunk.
I raised the boy she gave to God's service, and taught him to answer God's call.
My two greedy sons died on the same day, just as a man of God had foretold.
When I heard the ark of God had been captured, I fell backward off my seat and died.

question: Which army commander am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 3; 18; 1 Kings 2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joab No. 1')

clues: I was David's nephew and the chief of his army for most of his reign.
I killed Abner in revenge for the death of my brother Asahel.
Against the king's orders, I thrust three shafts into Absalom as he hung in the oak.
Solomon had me put to death at the altar for the blood I had shed.

question: Which foreign king am I?
reference: 2 Kings 8; 10; 13 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Hazael')

clues: The prophet Elisha wept as he looked at me, foreseeing the harm I would do to Israel.
My master sent me to ask that prophet whether he would recover from his sickness.
The next day I smothered him with a wet cloth and took the throne of Syria.
I oppressed Israel harshly through the days of Jehu and his son.

question: Which priest am I?
reference: 2 Kings 11; 2 Chronicles 24 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jehoiada No. 3')

clues: I hid an infant prince from a murderous queen for six years inside the temple.
In the seventh year I brought the boy out, crowned him, and had the queen executed.
I led the people to renew their covenant and to tear down the house of Baal.
I lived 130 years and was buried among the kings for the good I had done.

question: Which governor of Judah am I?
reference: Ezra 3-6; Haggai 1-2 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Zerubbabel')

clues: I led the first group of exiles back from Babylon to Jerusalem.
We rebuilt the altar and laid the temple's foundation, and the old men wept aloud.
Opposition halted the work until the prophets Haggai and Zechariah stirred us to start again.
The temple was completed in the sixth year of Darius.

question: Which missionary am I?
reference: Acts 15-16; 1 Thessalonians 1:1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Silas')

clues: I was a leading man in the Jerusalem congregation, sent to carry its letter to Antioch.
Paul chose me as his traveling companion after he and Barnabas parted ways.
At midnight, after an earthquake shook our prison, a jailer and his whole household were baptized.
I was a co-sender of both letters to the Thessalonians.

question: Which God-fearing officer am I?
reference: Acts 10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Cornelius')

clues: I was an army officer of the Italian band, stationed at Caesarea.
An angel told me that my prayers and my gifts of mercy had come up as a remembrance before God.
I sent men to fetch Peter, who came even though I was a Gentile.
The holy spirit fell on my whole household while Peter was still speaking.

question: Which capital city am I?
reference: 2 Samuel 5; 2 Kings 25; Luke 19 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jerusalem', p. 40)

clues: David captured me from the Jebusites and made me his royal city.
Solomon built the first temple on my Mount Moriah.
Nebuchadnezzar burned me and my temple to the ground.
Jesus wept over me and foretold that not one stone would be left upon another.

question: Which river am I?
reference: Joshua 3; 2 Kings 2; 5; Matthew 3 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jordan')

clues: My waters were cut off upstream so a nation could cross into the Promised Land on dry ground.
A Syrian commander dipped in me seven times and his leprosy was gone.
Two prophets in turn struck me with a rolled-up cloak and crossed on dry land.
John immersed crowds in me, including Jesus.

question: Which headland am I?
reference: 1 Kings 18 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Carmel No. 1')

clues: A lone prophet challenged 450 prophets of Baal on my slopes.
Fire fell from the heavens and consumed a sacrifice that had been drenched with water.
From my base the prophet then outran a chariot all the way to Jezreel.
A servant watching the sea from me spotted a small cloud that ended a long drought.

question: Which cunning judge am I?
reference: Judges 3:15-30 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ehud No. 1')

clues: I was sent to carry tribute to Eglon, the very fat king of Moab.
I had a short two-edged sword strapped under my clothing on my right thigh.
Telling the king I had a secret word from God, I drove the blade into him in his private chamber.
I slipped away, blew the horn in the hills, and led Israel to seize the fords against Moab.
